(p-287) Surah al-Kawthar

It is also called al-Nahr (the Sacrifice).

Its purpose is the bestowal of every good that can be. Its name al-Kawthar is clear in this regard, and likewise al-Nahr, since it is well known in the slaughtering of camels, and that is the utmost generosity among the Arabs.

"In the name of Allah" (bismillah), the Sovereign, the Greatest, the Most Generous, the Most Noble, [He] whose abundant bounty has no limit; "the Most Gracious" (al-Rahman), who encompassed all creation with His generosity and differentiated among them in the downpour of His rain; "the Most Merciful" (al-Rahim), who singled out His party for guidance by His guidance and for holding fast to His rope.

* *

Since Surah al-Din (Surah 107), by its explicit content, forbids the blameworthy traits of character, it, by its implications, calls to the lofty dispositions. Therefore al-Kawthar came for this purpose. Surah al-Din had concluded with the most miserly of the miserly and the lowest of creatures: withholding (al-man'), as a warning against stinginess and what it leads to of denial. So al-Kawthar begins with the most generous of generosity: giving to the most noble of creatures, as an encouragement toward it and an exhortation to it. It is as if it were said: "You, O best of creation, are not characterized by anything of what that concluding surah forbade, withholding small kindnesses (al-ma'un)." ﴿Inna﴾ (Indeed We), with what We possess of greatness, (p-288) and it is emphasized because of their denial: ﴿a'taynaka﴾ (We have given you), that is, We have bestowed upon you with great empowerment. He did not say "ataynaka" (We have brought you), because the root of ita' (giving) is bringing near, though it has become known in the sense of giving. ﴿al-Kawthar﴾ (the abundance), which is among the generosity bestowed upon those who affirm the Day of Judgment.

Since the abundance of a chief exceeds the abundance of others, how much more that of a king; how much more that of the King of kings; how much more when it is expressed in the form of intensification; how much more when it is manifested in the aspect of greatness; how much more when the form is built upon the vowel waw, which carries elevation and dominance; how much more when it comes after the fatha, which has the like of that [and even more] — rather, greater — the meaning is: We have poured upon you and made lawful for you from every thing, of substances and meanings, of knowledge and action and other things, from the mines of both abodes and their aids, a good that has no end, so it does not fall under description; and We have made you independent of having to prefer others with it or to accumulate your wealth by bringing benefit or repelling harm. Among it is the river in Paradise, and the Pool (al-Hawd) extended for the believers to drink from in the Gathering (al-Mahshar), whose likeness in this world is his Shari'ah (ﷺ), whose handholds and means are the number of the stars, who are the scholars of his community [those to be followed; thus there has gathered for you the two felicities: the most noble of gifts from the most generous of givers] and the greatest of them.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When He forbade His servants from what those who desire this world and its adornment delight in — from excessive accumulation, arrogance, glorying in wealth and rank, and pursuing worldly gain — He followed that with what He granted His Prophet, which is better than what they amass, namely al-Kawthar, which is abundant good. Among it is the Pool that his community will approach on the Day of Resurrection, whoever drinks from it will never thirst. Among it is his praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud), by which the first and the last will praise him at the time of his general intercession for creation and relief from the terror of the standing place. Among this good is what was prepared for him in his life: the permitting of spoils, victory through awe, and great character, and countless other goods of both the worldly and the Hereafter, some of which are better than this world and what is in it, since this world and what is in it are not equal to a single one of these gifts. ﴿Say: By the grace of Allah and His mercy — in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾ [Yunus: 58]. And among the al-Kawthar and the good that Allah gave him is His Clear Book, which gathers the intellect of the first and the last, and is a healing for what is in the breasts.

When He, glory be to Him, completed for him of blessings what cannot be enumerated, and of which the lowest is not comparable to the worldly delights in their entirety, He said, explaining and alerting to the greatness of what He gave him:

﴿Do not extend your eyes toward what We have provided to some pairs of them﴾ [al-Hijr: 88] up to His saying ﴿and the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾ [Ta-Ha: 131]. Thus the blessing of al-Kawthar, which was given to him, has dwarfed every bounty Allah the Exalted mentioned in the Book of the people of this world, and whoever among them was established. This is one of the reasons for placing this surah (p-290) after it: nothing of the delights of this world is mentioned after it, nor any of those who enjoy them, because this purpose has concluded and been completed. Surah al-Din was the last to contain an allusion to something of that, as was mentioned earlier in the introduction to its allusions. And with this the reason for its being placed after it becomes clear — and Allah knows best. End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 108, verse 2:

When He had given him that by which He freed him for worship and granted him a richness that needs nothing else, He made the following statement its consequence, commanding him with what comprises all the aspects of gratitude: ﴿So pray﴾, that is, by cutting off attachments to creatures, by standing before Allah in the presence of watchfulness (muraqabah), thankful for the beneficence of the Bestower, unlike one who is heedless of it and one who shows off in it.

And when He brought the manifestation of greatness (al-'azamah) in order to multiply the giving, the command with what belongs to the King of loftiness followed from it. His command ﷺ was creative (takwini), with which there is no refusal, so there occurred a shift (iltifat) to the attribute of beneficence, which calls for encouragement and approach, because of what it conveys of endearment, along with explicit mention of Tawhid, and the indication that worship does not occur except as gratitude. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿To your Lord﴾, that is, the One who has done good to you in this, secretly and openly, defying whoever you wish, so that no one has any way over you. ﴿And sacrifice﴾, that is, spend for Him from wealth, al-Kawthar, upon the needy, unlike the one who pushes away the orphan and does not urge the feeding of the poor, and withholds small kindnesses (al-Ma'un). This is because nahr (sacrifice of the camel) is the best of the expenditures of the Arabs, since a single she-camel suffices a hundred poor persons, and when the Arabs use the word "wealth" without qualification, it refers to camels. For this reason He expressed this meaning by nahr, so that the prohibition is understood against what they used to do of slaughtering for the idols. Among its meanings also is manifesting humility, lowliness and submissiveness in the prayer by placing the right hand upon the left beneath the nahr, in the posture of one who is humble and submissive. In this He has matched four things from Surah al-Din (107) with four: stinginess in giving, neglecting the prayer by commanding it, showing off by restricting it to the Lord, and withholding zakat by the nahr.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 108, verse 3 (part 1 of 2):

When He commanded him to devote time entirely to the worship of the Creator and to show kindness to creation through the best of creation, He gave a reason whose sum is that he has no preoccupation and no need at all that could distress him. So He said: ﴿Indeed, your enemy﴾, that is, the one who hates you, who disavows you and who belittles you, despite what you have been given of beauty, praiseworthy qualities and perfection, ﴿is the one cut off﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿the one cut off﴾: cut off from his origin, cut off in offspring, destitute, cut off from good, blessing and remembrance. No one comes after him who takes up his cause and is mentioned through him, even if he gathered wealth and freed his body for every kind of beauty. You are the one whose affair is connected, whose name is renowned and whose rank is exalted. So do not turn toward them in any way, for they are too insignificant for the one who has emptied himself to win the honour of standing in our noble presence and of taking pride in dwelling at our lofty and sublime thresholds to care about them. For you is what you are upon, and for them is what they are in. Thus the final verse is the conclusion, because from al-Kawthar comes the exaltation of his affair, and the affair of his lovers and followers in the dominion of the heavens and the earth and the river of Paradise, and the lowliness of the standing of his enemy in both. Its joints have thus been bound together, as you see, with its connection; its last part is known from its first; and it is known that its middle is like the middle joints, embracing the first by being from its fruits, and connected to the last because it is from the ends of its course. God has spoken truthfully, and who is more truthful in speech than God? No remembrance through a son or a follower remains for any of his haters, nor is there any thankful one, praiser or exalter of them found [for them].

As for him ﷺ, his offspring have filled the earth from Fatimah al-Zahra, and they are the most honourable, despite the extreme efforts of kings to kill them and to empty the earth of their progeny, out of fear of their lofty honour over their own honour, and their elevation through humility [that prevails] over their arrogance. When you review the verse: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of God﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40], from surah al-Ahzab, you will know that the death of his sons, peace be upon them, before him was part of raising his rank and increasing his honour through the singling out of his remembrance. As for his followers, they have taken possession of most of the earth, and they are the people of the criterion, of brilliant knowledge and of gnosis. It is also derived from this that whoever empties himself for his Lord, God destroys his enemy and suffices him against each one of them.

It is known that the sum of this surah is the bestowal upon him ﷺ of the great good, of which the flowing river from Paradise is part, at the gathering place for those who follow him, and which is forbidden to those who turn away from him and cut themselves off from him. He is commanded to pray and to sacrifice, for expanding provision to the needy, and given the good news of cutting off the root of his enemies and of the victory of the group of his allies. Just as one of the aims of surah al-A'raf is that it is a counterpart to it, in returning the ending to the beginning, there is the warning to the wrongdoers of destruction in His saying: ﴿And how many a town have We destroyed﴾ [al-A'raf: 4] and so on, and the depiction of that through the mention of the fates of those who preceded them for opposing the Messengers, peace and blessings be upon them; and the command to prayer, covering the nakedness, and what is intended by sacrifice, in His saying: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of worship, and eat and drink﴾ [al-A'raf: 31] and the verses that follow. He also mentions who is granted the water of Paradise and who is prevented from it, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water or of what God has provided you"﴾ [al-A'raf: 50] and the verses that follow; and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our signs﴾ [al-A'raf: 156], ﴿who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written with them﴾ [al-A'raf: 157] and the verses that follow. This is what relates to the explanation of its structures and its sentences, and the interpretation of its details and its summaries, and likewise its counterpart in the beginnings of its affair and its completion.

Then this surah consists of ten words in writing, indicating that the completion of the cutting off of his hater would be with the completion of the tenth year of the Hijra (migration), and so it was. The eleventh year of the Hijra had not passed while in the Arabian Peninsula, anyone who sees the noblest of his states, which is spending himself and his wealth for his love, [had remained]. If we add to them the two hidden pronouns they become twelve. In the twelfth year of prophethood, the Ansar pledged allegiance to him ﷺ [to confront the disbelievers. If the five explicit pronouns are added to the ten words, they become fifteen, indicating that] at the completion of the fifteenth year of his prophethood he ﷺ would extend his lofty hand to cut off his enemies, and so it was at the battle of Badr, of lofty rank. In the hidden pronouns was the pledge, and it was hidden; in the explicit pronouns was Badr, and it was famous. When the two hidden pronouns are added to that, they become seventeen. In the seventeenth year of his prophethood was the battle of Badr, the appointed encounter, and the Prophet ﷺ made the promise to come to Badr to meet the Quraysh for fighting and for the clash of champions. God made them aware, so they did not come. The events after the Hijra were considered among the states of prophethood [when the ten written words were counted, because they are the strongest states of prophethood], just as the written words are stronger than the pronouns, though all share the name of words. Therefore the complete cutting off of the hater was taken as what occurred in the eleventh year, namely the destruction of the people of apostasy and the steadfastness of the Arabs in the attribute of Islam. When the five explicit pronouns, which are closer than the hidden ones, were combined with the written words [and weaker than the written words], he considered [the beginning of] the surah, for the appropriateness of the weakness of the state that was before the Hijra, and so this corresponds to the second year of the Hijra in which the great battle of Badr took place. Although it was of great magnitude and very significant, it was in a manner contrary to what was expected, for the state of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, was at its weakest then. And because it was the first victory among the campaigns, the souls of the opponents were not submissive, since what follows it would be like it. When the two hidden pronouns are added to that, and they are weaker [than] the explicit ones, the number fits the year of the battle of Badr, the appointed encounter, in the fourth year. Though it was strong, because the Quraysh were too weak to meet, [its state was weaker than Badr, in which fighting took place, and more concealed].

That its written words and its technical words, which are parts of the written words, are seventeen indicates that the command in ﴿So pray﴾ [al-Kawthar: 2] is directed in essence, primarily, to the five daily prayers, which are seventeen units [of prayer], and that whoever persists in them [is] one who prays and is outside the obligation of the command. When you intend, [during] travel, what the attribute of nurturing through kindness requires, the number decreases by the number of pronouns, apart from the one whose command is fulfilled by them, because a command arising from a manifestation of greatness does not admit reduction in itself, since it is the word of command. When we add to them the four words of the basmalah (the invocation "In the name of God..."), it has great secrets from another aspect. That is because the written words become fourteen, indicating that the beginning of the cutting off of opposites occurs with a power close to action, through preparation for it in the fourteenth year of prophethood, which is the year of the Hijra. When we add to them the explicit pronouns, which are closer to the written words and are five, they become nineteen. In the nineteenth year of prophethood, which is the sixth year of the Hijra, was the manifest conquest over the two haters, in which God sent down the surah of al-Fath (the Victory). When we add to them the two hidden pronouns they become twenty-one, which is the eighth year of the Hijra, the year of the Great Conquest, in which knowledge became general that the hater is the one cut off. If their letters are counted as pronounced, they are forty-four letters. If you match them with the years from the beginning of the time of prophethood, the last of them is the thirty-first year of the Hijra, which is the year of the Greatest Cutting Off of his greatest hater, who tore up his book and who owned the lands of Yemen, a large part of the lands of the Arabs and likewise of others close to his lands. The Quraysh used to count him among them, as has been explained in surah al-Rum. He is Kisra, king of the Persians. [In that year came the end of their kingdom with the killing of their last king, Yazdajird]. Just as when you consider its written words together with the explicit pronouns, which are technical words, apart from what is hidden (the obligation of its being hidden prevents whoever counts it), they are nineteen words. If they are considered with this, they correspond to the time of the death of Caesar, tyrant of the Romans, in the nineteenth year of the Hijra, whom God destroyed, who had equipped himself in person to fight the Arabs at Alexandria and had commanded that none of the Romans stay behind him. God broke the power of the Romans by his death, and the Arabs became bold at that time. Thus the letters indicated the cutting off of the hater from the Persians, and the words indicated the cutting off of the hater from the Romans. [The indication through the letters is more appropriate for the Persians and Romans] because they are not people of knowledge, and the Romans are [indicated] by the words because they are people of knowledge, and words are closer to knowledge.

When the pronounced letters of the basmalah are counted, they are eighteen letters. If you make them years from the beginning of prophethood, the last of them is the fifth year of the Hijra, in which was the battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). After they withdrew from it, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Now we will attack them and they will not attack us." This was the first taking of the hater into being cut off. When you consider the letters according to the written form, they are nineteen, the last of which is the sixth year, which was the Umrah of Hudaybiyya, the year of the causal conquest, which is the treaty in which surah al-Fath was revealed, and God called it a conquest. The Prophet ﷺ said: "It is the greatest of conquests." [So it was the cause of the greatest conquest through the mingling of the disbelievers with the people of Islam through the treaty, and they hastened to enter Islam, because of what they saw of the excellence of the religion and the inimitability of the Qur'an. On the day of the conquest they were ten thousand, after they had been, two years before, on the day of Hudaybiyya, one thousand four hundred.] And God is the Granter of success.

This is a small part of the secrets of this surah, and from it is known some of its inimitability, which expands the hearts and delights the eyes, for it surpasses in beauty the luxuriant gardens. It is also known the madness of the wicked buffoon Musaylima the Liar, may the curse and perdition of God be upon him, and his is the evil of the final return and destination, when he said in opposing it: "We have given you the abundance, so pray to your Lord and withdraw. Indeed, your hater is the one who is cut off." Because it is speech, though it is short in reach, weak in its texture and warp, drowned in its open field and its end in destruction and annihilation, having no richness in it, rather all of it is toil and exertion, loose in weave, decayed in strength, its bonds broken, its sides loosened, corrupt in meaning and structure, base in its words, bitter in its fruit, because the causes are contrary to what they cause, and the all-encompassing is discordant with what is encompassed. Then I saw in Dala'il al-I'jaz (Proofs of Inimitability) of the Imam Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani that the middle [of his words] is one who said: "the adulterer" and "he openly defied," and if it is by religion, it does not prevent proclaiming falsehood, and no sensible person approves of that; and if it is by war, it is on equal terms for everyone who reflects and understands. There is no text in it on victory for its two objectives, nor a demand [that is achieved], with deficiency in generosity in every case, which is the aim for the rich and the poor, the commanded and the commander. This is together with the raid upon the style and the imitation of what is familiar, not escaping [from it]

in the retribution there is life (Qur'an 2:179) — in the dropping of "killing is more deterrent against killing," with the nimbleness of brevity and the sweetness together with eloquence, in a hit that reaches the very meaning, in a way that leads to willingness to give up the soul and moves one to hasten to obey the command. And the first, from the foolish intellect of the sunken-eyed one and his eating... to creation, with the lack of meaning that is concealed for secrecy? And the other neglects those with doubts and concealment, along with what it missed of limiting the loss and the specific ruin, and what it contains of clarifying the cutting lie that destroys lifetimes and ruins homes, confirming the Prophet ﷺ, the righteous, by the hands of his noble companions. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of insight (Qur'an 59:2). So glory be to Him whose act is exalted, whose speech is above every speech, and peace and praise be to God in every state.
